extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: Open-source datasets for training reasoning models, composed of science, math, and code data.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, Ashima Suvama, Benjamin Feuer, Liangyu Chen, Zaid Khan, Eric Frankel, Sachin Grover, Caroline Choi, Niklas Muennighoff, Shiye Su, Wanjia Zhao, John Yang, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Kartik Sharma, Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji, Yichuan Deng, Sarah Pratt, Vivek Ramanujan, Jon Saad-Falcon, Jeffrey Li, Achal Dave, Alon Albalak, Kushal Arora, Blake Wulfe, Chinmay Hegde, Greg Durrett, Sewoong Oh, Mohit Bansal, Saadia Gabriel, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Vaishaal Shankar, Aaron Gokaslan, Mike A. Merrill, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Yejin Choi, Jenia Jitsev, Reinhard Heckel, Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection pipeline involves sourcing questions from fully synthetic, semi-synthetic, and non-synthetic sources across math, code, and science domains.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from 27 different sources for code, 21 for math, and 14 for science.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was decontaminated against evaluation benchmarks by removing samples with high similarity using Indel similarity and N-gram-based similarity metrics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers were generated using a teacher model (QwQ-32B) with 16 answers sampled per question.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not explore reinforcement learning and does not use staged SFT or curriculum learning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training reasoning models via supervised finetuning (SFT).

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The first step in our data generation pipeline is finding questions for each data domain. We can broadly categorize our question sourcing techniques into three types: (1) Fully synthetic... (2) Semi-synthetic... (3) Non-synthetic...

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We can broadly categorize our question sourcing techniques into three types: (1) Fully synthetic – an existing LLM generates questions with little-to-no seed material... (2) Semi-synthetic – an LLM uses existing data sources such as CommonCrawl or FineWeb... (3) Non-synthetic – humans write the questions. Examples include StackExchange and ShareGPTCode.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Our experiments cover 27 different question sources for code questions, 21 sources for math, and 14 sources for science.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We also decontaminate our datasets against our benchmarks by removing samples with high similarity.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Our final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains... We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Our final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: This work has several limitations. We did not explore datasets for reinforcement leaming, a standard training regime for building reasoning models. Within the SFT realm, we did not explore the use of staged SFT or curriculum leaming to further improve performance.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The goal of the OpenThoughts project is to create open-source datasets for training reasoning models.
